Subject: Post-call recap + next steps for Acme evals

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: Validate model fit for Acme’s customer support summarization and policy‑answering workflows; prioritize precision and low hallucination.
- Minimum success criteria: >= 92% factual accuracy on the 500-sample holdout and hallucination rate < 3% (see scoring below).
- Suggested models to evaluate initially: Llama 2 70B (q4f16), MiniRedwood-13B (optimized fp16), and Redwood-optimized Llama-65B-q4 (our curated runtime profile).
- Data format: CSV with columns [id, prompt, reference, split, metadata]. I attached a sample promptset with formatting notes.
- Next steps:
  1) You upload the eval promptset (or grant us a shared Drive link).
  2) We’ll spin up an eval job on Redwood Dedicated with the three model variants and identical sampling seeds.
  3) We’ll return a side-by-side report (accuracy, hallucination, response length, latency) and recommend a production candidate.

Attachments: acmefin_eval_promptset.csv, redwood_eval_setup_guide.pdf

Action items for Acme: please share the full CSV (500-1,000 rows preferred) and flag any PII rows you want excluded or masked. If it’s easier, upload to the Drive folder I shared and reply with the link.

I’m cc’ing Avery to handle the eval orchestration and Dev for any dataset/format questions.

Thanks —

Thanks — good questions. Answers inline and more detail on the eval setup: 

1) Reference columns: please include two columns if possible: human_summary, canonical_answer. The human_summary helps for qualitative checks; canonical_answer is used for automated scoring. If only one is available, canonical_answer is sufficient.

2) Hallucination metric: we use a hybrid approach — automated flagging (entity overlap, factual checks against the canonical answer) followed by a targeted human review for flagged items. For this eval we recommend a 10% random human audit of flagged responses to validate the automated detector. This keeps cost down but catches subtle mistakes.

3) Timeline: EOD Friday ET is feasible. We’ll queue the run and aim to return first-pass results by Monday morning PST.

Eval setup on Redwood (high level):
- Upload: Upload CSV to the shared Drive folder or provide a pre-signed S3 link. File naming: acmefin_eval_promptset.csv
- Config: In the Redwood Console evals page pick the three model variants (Llama 2 70B q4f16, Redwood-optimized Llama-65B-q4, MiniRedwood-13B fp16). Set deterministic seed, max_tokens=512, temperature=0.0 for canonical scoring runs.
- Metrics: exact-match / token-F1 for structured answers, BLEU/ROUGE for summaries, hallucination_rate (automated), response_length, avg_latency. We’ll also produce a preference-based A/B if you want pairwise human judgements for top candidates.
- Scoring criteria (initial):
  • Accuracy (canonical_answer match): pass if >= 92%
  • Hallucination rate: fail if > 3%
  • Latency: median p50 < 350ms for customer-critical paths (we’ll measure across Dedicated config)
  • Regression guard: compare to baseline (we’ll use our prior eval of Llama 2 70B on the same prompts). Any drop > 2% accuracy or increase > 0.5% hallucination triggers an investigation.

Notes on model selection: the Llama 2 70B q4f16 often strikes the best accuracy/latency balance here, but Redwood-optimized Llama-65B-q4 may outperform on hallucination depending on prompt engineering. MiniRedwood-13B is primarily a cost-reduction candidate for lower-criticality paths.

Action items from our side:
- We’ll prepare the eval job and share a Console link where you can track progress.
- Dev: can you double-check the sample CSV attached for required header names and a short script to convert Acme’s internal JSON export into the CSV format?

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Avery/Marissa — attaching a quick conversion checklist and a one‑liner script we’ll run if Acme provides JSON instead of CSV. Key notes:

- Required CSV headers: id, prompt, human_summary, canonical_answer, split (train/holdout), metadata.tags
- For policy/PII: we’ll apply Redwood’s redaction pipeline by default if Acme marks rows as pii=true in metadata. Otherwise leave them as-is.
- Script: python script will normalize newlines, strip HTML, and ensure UTF-8; we’ll also enforce seed deterministic shuffling for splits.
- Devops note: for Dedicated runs we’ll reserve a small burst pool to hit latency targets during the run; should be transparent to Acme.

I’ll start the job once Sarah confirms the upload link.
